newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas holds on weather, storage refills.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas holds on weather, storage refills.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly steady Tuesday as cooler-than-normal weather in most of the East and Midwest and continued storage injections sustained demand, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices held in the mid-to-high $1.90s, with Transco (Station 65) still quoted at $2.00-2.05 and Henry Hub at $1.98-2.01 per mmBtu.

Prices in south Texas were also steady in the low-to-mid $1.90s. A gradual rise in temperatures is expected this week throughout most of the state, which may put some downward pressure on prices later this week.
At the New York city-gate, prices slipped five cents to about $2.30-2.35 despite forecasts for even cooler weather later this week in the region.
In congruence with Gulf values, Appalachian prices were mostly steady at $2.18-2.20 on Columbia and mid-$2.20s on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, prices were flat to about one cent lower at $1.84-$1.86, with Demarcation quoted in the low-$1.90s.
Chicago city-gate prices were also talked about one cent lower at $2.10-2.11.
Traders blamed the standstill in prices on moderating temperatures in the region. Near- to slightly below-normal temperatures are forecast to last through the week, Weather Services Corp said.

Further west, Permian basin prices held in the mid-to-high $1.80s as storage injections continued at a fairly steady pace. Waha values were quoted at $1.90-1.93, while southern California border prices were little changed at $1.97-1.99.
The 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit remained shut for refueling, while Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 MW Diablo 2 nuclear unit resumed full power output.
